record.original_question: Let A⊆N. For a positive increasing unbounded function h on R_+, define lower and upper h-densities of a set X by liminf and limsup of h(X(n))/h(n), where X(n) is the counting function of X. The exponential density is the special case h(x)=log x. Characterize the exponential-density set R_exp(A)={(upper_exp(B), lower_exp(B)): B⊆A} for a fixed set A.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{N}=\{1,2,3,\dots\}$. For a set $X\subseteq\mathbb{N}$, let $X(n)=|X\cap[1,n]|$ denote its counting function. Given a positive, increasing, unbounded function $h:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, define the lower and upper $h$-densities of $X$ by
$$\underline{d}_h(X)=\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{h(X(n))}{h(n)},\qquad \overline{d}_h(X)=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{h(X(n))}{h(n)}.$$
When $h(x)=\log x$, the resulting densities are called the lower and upper exponential densities, denoted $\underline{d}_{\exp}(X)$ and $\overline{d}_{\exp}(X)$.

For a fixed set $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$, define
$$R_{\exp}(A)=\bigl\{\,(\overline{d}_{\exp}(B),\,\underline{d}_{\exp}(B)) : B\subseteq A\,\bigr\}\subseteq[0,1]^2.$$

Characterize the set $R_{\exp}(A)\subseteq[0,1]^2$ as $A$ varies over subsets of $\mathbb{N}$; equivalently, describe explicitly, for each fixed $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$, which pairs $(\beta,\alpha)\in[0,1]^2$ with $\alpha\le\beta$ are realized as $(\overline{d}_{\exp}(B),\underline{d}_{\exp}(B))$ for some $B\subseteq A$.
artifact.status_search_result: The general characterization of the exponential density set $R_{\exp}(A)$ for arbitrary fixed $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ appears to remain open. Partial progress exists: work by Grekos and collaborators relates upper exponential density to limit ratios (e.g., upper limit ratio less than 1 forces upper exponential density 0), and a 2020 paper by Leonetti–Miska in Mediterr. J. Math. on exponential densities and limit ratios establishes realizability results for prescribed values of the lower/upper exponential density together with limit ratios, answering related open questions of Grekos et al. A full characterization of $R_{\exp}(A)$ for every fixed $A$ has not been located.

status_evidence.title: On Exponential Densities and Limit Ratios of Subsets of N
status_evidence.snippet: There exists a subset of N such that its lower and upper exponential densities and its lower and upper limit ratios can take prescribed values, providing an affirmative answer to an open problem posed by Grekos et al.
status_evidence.claim: Partial realizability results are known for prescribed exponential density values, but a full characterization of R_exp(A) for fixed A is not stated as solved.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotic ψ-densities of subsets of natural numbers
status_evidence.snippet: The paper studies asymptotic ψ-densities (generalizing logarithmic and other densities) but does not address the full characterization of R_exp(A).
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on generalized densities does not resolve the characterization of R_exp(A).
